problem: It says the two colours are 'equally bright' because both have V = 0.7843. V is only the largest channel value, not perceived brightness. Two colours with the same V can look very different in lightness, so a student may generalise 'same V = same brightness'.
fix: Say: 'Both have the same V = 0.78, so HSV calls them equally valued. Note that V is the maximum channel, not perceived lightness; judged by eye the red and the blue need not look equally bright.'

problem: It says 'CMY stores the three inks a printer lays down', but the chapter itself explains that printers use four inks (CMYK). A student skimming the lead may think a printer uses only three.
fix: Say: 'CMY stores the three subtractive inks; real printers add a black ink K and work in CMYK.'

problem: The title spells the word 'Color' while the whole body uses 'colour'. Mixed spelling looks careless in an exam answer.
fix: Use one spelling throughout, e.g. keep the syllabus word in the title and 'colour' in the body, or write 'Colour models such as RGB, CMY and HSV'.
